class.name: FellowWater3D
class.brief_description: A body of water (lake, river, sea) with spectral wind waves, drawn to the horizon (FellowEngine).
class.description: The surface of a body of water at the node's height, to the horizon or within [member extent]. Wind waves are simulated on the GPU after Tessendorf: a JONSWAP spectrum (wind speed and fetch) with the Donelan-Banner spreading, evolved and transformed by FFT every frame in up to four cascades of different tile lengths ([member cascade_lengths]); the surface is displaced by them and shaded with their slopes. Where a [FellowShallowWater3D] covers the body ([member simulation_path]), its simulated surface is blended in: its height, its slopes and foam, and its flow carries the waves (flow mapping). Shading (one transparent material): reflections traced in screen space against the opaque scene, with the screen's view of distant scenery and the sky's IBL where nothing near is hit; Fresnel; refraction of the scene below through the screen texture; absorption along the light's path down and the view's path up ([member absorption]); in-scattering ([member scattering_color]) lit by the scene's lights, shadows included; foam from breaking waves (where the surface folds), shores ([member shore_foam_depth]) and the simulation; caustics on the refracted bottom computed from the waves' own slopes; the sun's highlight with a roughness that grows with the slope variance a pixel does not resolve, so a far surface shows a glitter path rather than a mirror image. The surface mesh is a polar grid around the camera; its displacement is band-limited to the grid's spacing. The node's rotation and scale are not used; [member extent] is axis-aligned. Needs the Forward+ or Mobile renderer; [code]rendering/fellow/fluid/enabled[/code] off stops the waves (the surface keeps its last state). Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0123-water.md[/code]. In the editor the waves move as in the running game; the 3D editor's toolbar toggle [b]Animate[/b] (the editor setting [code]editors/3d/fellow/animate_nodes[/code]) off stills them, and the editor then redraws only when something changes (milestone 52).

method.name: add_foam
method.description: Adds foam on the surface around a point (world): [param amount] at the centre, less outwards, none at [param radius] metres; a place holds at most [code]1.0[/code] (as covered as the foam's pattern gets). It fades by [member body_foam_decay] and is drawn within [member body_foam_size] of the camera (outside it, nothing is added). [FellowBuoyancy3D] adds the foam of bodies splashing in and moving through the water; a game can add an explosion's, a character's wading, a boat's.

method.name: add_wake_sound
method.description: Adds to this frame's sound of water moving past a body near a point (world): [param level] is the waterline's length times how fast the water passes it (m²/s; a 2 m raft pushed at 3 m/s about 4). Called every physics tick while it lasts (the level is the frame's mean over its ticks; wakes within 4 m share a voice); it fades out 50 ms after the calls stop. [FellowBuoyancy3D] calls it for its body.

method.name: debug_compare_cpu_waves
method.description: The waves on the CPU (see [method get_surface_height]) against the GPU's displacement texture for a cascade, at the texels the CPU's grid has, at the time of the last GPU update: [code]height_rms[/code], [code]height_error_rms[/code], [code]height_error_max[/code], [code]dx_rms[/code], [code]dx_error_rms[/code] (metres), [code skip-lint]time[/code] (of the GPU's update). Synchronous: for tests.

method.name: debug_get_displacement_image
method.description: The displacement of a cascade as computed on the GPU (x, y, z, foam; with mipmaps). Synchronous: for tests.

method.name: debug_get_spectrum_image
method.description: The initial spectrum of a cascade as uploaded (h0(k), conj(h0(-k))): for tests against a reference.

method.name: debug_render_sound
method.description: The sound's synthesis offline, mono at [param rate] for [param seconds]: [param events] (by time) are dictionaries — [code]{time, speed, size[, gain]}[/code] a splash, [code]{time, wake}[/code] the wake's level from then, [code]{time, bubble, amplitude[, rise]}[/code] one bubble of that radius (metres). For tests and tuning (see [code]benchmarks/tools/buoyancy/water_sound.gd[/code]).

method.name: get_body_foam_stats
method.description: The foam added with [method add_foam] (and by [FellowBuoyancy3D]): [code]active[/code] (any left), [code]cells[/code] (cells of its grid with foam), [code]total[/code] (their amounts' sum), [code]cell_size[/code] (metres), [code]centre[/code] (the grid's centre, world x and z), [code]frames[/code] and [code]usec_per_frame[/code] (the main thread's time fading it and sending it to the GPU, in the frames with foam).

method.name: get_cpu_wave_stats
method.description: The waves on the CPU: [code]updates[/code], [code]usec_per_update[/code] (their mean CPU time), [code]threaded_updates[/code] (made on a worker thread), [code]main_usec_per_update[/code] (the main thread's mean time in updates and in waiting for the worker's), [code]builds[/code] and [code]usec_per_build[/code] (the modes, made again when the spectrum changes), [code]height_rms[/code] (the CPU's waves' rms height before [member wave_scale], metres), [code]variance_share[/code] (the share of the waves' variance they hold), [code]grid[/code] (the first cascade's grid side).

method.name: get_displacement_texture
method.description: The cascades' displacement (x, y, z in metres; foam in alpha), one layer per cascade, with mipmaps.

method.name: get_foam
method.description: The foam added with [method add_foam] (and by [FellowBuoyancy3D]) at a point (world): [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]; [code]0.0[/code] outside the square of [member body_foam_size] around the camera.

method.name: get_significant_wave_height
method.description: The significant wave height (four times the standard deviation of the surface) of the configured spectrum, in metres.

method.name: get_slope_texture
method.description: The cascades' slopes (sx, sz, sx², sz²), one layer per cascade, with mipmaps.

method.name: get_sound_stats
method.description: The sound: [code]voices[/code], [code]playing[/code], [code]splashes[/code] (played), [code]merged[/code] (joined a voice sounding near them), [code]stolen[/code] (took the quietest voice), [code]dropped[/code] (too far from the listener, or quieter than every voice), [code]bubbles[/code] (synthesised), [code]bubbles_dropped[/code], [code]active_bubbles[/code], [code]peak_bubbles[/code] (most at once in a voice), [code]mixed_seconds[/code] and [code]mix_usec_per_second[/code] (the audio thread's time a second of sound, all voices).

method.name: get_surface_ceiling
method.description: A height (world) the waves on the CPU stay under: the water's level plus six times their rms height. A body whose lowest point is above it is out of the water without the waves being evaluated ([FellowBuoyancy3D] skips such a tick).

method.name: get_surface_height
method.description: The height (world) of the surface over a point (world), as drawn: the longer waves (cascades of 10 m and more, each up to 32 of its fundamentals; in a sea of 2.3 m significant wave height 1.3 cm rms off the GPU's surface) evaluated on the CPU from the GPU's own modes, the horizontal displacement inverted. [code]-INF[/code] outside [member extent]. The CPU's waves are transformed for the time of each frame on a worker thread (about 0.3-0.4 ms) after the frame's process, while something asked for the surface in the frame before; asked for at another time (the first frame, a [member time] set by hand), they are transformed at once. [FellowBuoyancy3D] floats bodies on it. The surface blended with a [FellowShallowWater3D] is not included.

method.name: get_surface_mesh_instance
method.description: The internal mesh instance that draws the surface.

method.name: get_surface_velocity
method.description: The water's velocity at the surface over a point (world): the waves' orbital motion (the height's rate of change, the horizontal displacement's change since the CPU's last update).

method.name: get_waves_gpu_time_ms
method.description: GPU time of the waves' compute passes in the last measured frame (RenderingDevice timestamps).

method.name: play_splash
method.description: Plays the sound of something [param size] metres across striking the water at [param speed] m/s at a point (world): a slap, the bubbles it entrains ringing, and for a large or fast body its cavity closing. [FellowBuoyancy3D] plays its body's; a game can play a character's dive or a shell's impact. Nothing farther than [member sound_max_distance] from the listener.

members.member: Absorption per metre for red, green and blue light. Pure water absorbs red (0.45); dissolved matter absorbs blue (the default is a temperate lake's greenish water).
How fast the foam added by [method add_foam] (splashes, wakes) fades, per second (exponentially: half of it in 2.3 s with [code]0.3[/code]).

The side, in metres, of the square around the camera where foam added by [method add_foam] (splashes, wakes) is kept and drawn: a grid of 256 × 256 cells (0.25 m with [code]64.0[/code]) that follows the camera. [code]0.0[/code]: none. While there is none, nothing is computed or sent; while there is, about 20 µs of the main thread a frame and a 64 KB texture update.
Tile lengths of the wave cascades in metres, longest first; a zero ends the list. Each cascade holds the waves from six of its own fundamentals to where the next one starts.
The two depths at which the caustics are computed; the bottom interpolates between them.
Strength of the caustics on the refracted bottom (0 = off). They come from the cascades of at most 12 m.
Horizontal displacement of the waves (sharper crests, broader troughs). 0 = sine-like waves.
Shows one of the shading's terms instead of the water.
Size of the water's rectangle centred on the node (x and z, in metres). Zero: to the horizon.
Distance over which the wind has blown over water, in kilometres: a small lake's waves are short, the open sea's long.
Period of the flow mapping that carries the waves with the simulation's flow (two phases half a period apart).
Albedo of the foam.
Rate at which breaking waves' foam fades (1/s).
Foam produced where the surface folds, per unit of the Jacobian below [member whitecap_threshold], per sixtieth of a second.
Radius of the surface's grid around the camera, in metres.
Radius of the grid's innermost ring, in metres.
Segments of each ring of the grid (the rings grow by 1 + 2π / segments, so its cells stay square).
With [member wind_from_scene], how much the scene wind's gusts roughen the shortest waves (0: not at all).

Length of the screen-space reflection rays of the linear march, in metres (the hierarchical one, with the depth texture's mip levels, follows a ray across the whole screen). Where nothing is hit, what the screen shows in the ray's direction is reflected if it is farther than this.
Below this Fresnel factor (looking down into the water) no reflection ray is traced: the sky's IBL alone (faded in over 1.5 times it).

Most steps of a screen-space reflection ray. With the depth texture's nearest-depth mip levels ([code]rendering/fellow/postfx/depth_copy_nearest_mipmaps[/code], on) the ray crosses the screen hierarchically, a cell of a level per step, up to twice this many steps; without them about one step per 10 pixels of its length on the screen, at least 6, quadratically spaced from a per-pixel offset, then refined by bisection.
How far the waves shift the scene seen below, relative to the water's thickness and the distance (0 = no refraction).
The waves repeat exactly after this many seconds (the dispersion relation is quantized to it): precise phases however long the clock runs.
Roughness of the surface below the waves' finest scale; the waves the pixel does not resolve add to it.
Albedo of the light scattered back by the water's body (lit by the scene's lights).
Trace reflections against the opaque scene's depth. Off: only the sky's IBL is reflected.
Depth below which shores and objects in the water get foam, in metres.
Width of the band along the simulation's edges in which its surface blends into the body's, in metres.
A [FellowShallowWater3D] whose simulated surface this node draws where it covers the body (its own mesh is hidden). It must be axis-aligned.
Scale of the wind waves inside the simulation (they also fade in water shallower than 60 cm).
The audio bus the water's voices play on.

If [code]true[/code], splashes and wakes ([method play_splash], [method add_wake_sound], [FellowBuoyancy3D]) are heard: synthesised from the physics of the air bubbles they entrain (each ringing at its Minnaert frequency, 3.26 m/s over its radius, damped by its losses, its pitch rising as it nears the surface — van den Doel's model), with no samples, on the audio thread, in [member sound_voices] 3D voices made at the first sound. A water nothing strikes makes no sound and costs nothing.
Sounds farther than this from the listener (the viewport's [AudioListener3D], else its camera) are not played; the voices' [member AudioStreamPlayer3D.max_distance].
The voices' [member AudioStreamPlayer3D.unit_size]: the distance at which they are heard at their full level.
How many sounds play at once: a splash joins a voice sounding within 2.5 m of it, else takes a free one, else the quietest if it is louder.
The voices' volume.
The [DirectionalLight3D] whose direction the caustics use. Empty: the scene's first visible directional light.
The waves' clock in seconds (not saved): advanced by the process time with [member time_auto], or set here for deterministic playback.
Advance the waves' clock with the process time. Off: set it yourself (deterministic playback).
Grid of each cascade (64, 128, 256 or 512 texels per side).
Scale of the waves' height and slopes.
Jacobian of the horizontal displacement below which breaking waves make foam (1 = flat; lower = fewer whitecaps).
Direction the wind blows towards, in degrees (0 = +X, 90 = +Z).

If [code]true[/code] and the scene has a [FellowWind3D], the waves follow its wind: [member wind_speed] and [member wind_direction] follow its speed and direction (the spectrum rebuilt when they change by 2 % or a degree), and its gusts roughen the shortest waves by [member gust_ripples] — darker, rougher water in a gust, a mirror in a lull.
Wind speed 10 m above the water, in m/s.
